source_review.review: Read discussion/conclusions and Fig9 caption, particularly printed pp41–44. Fig9 combines root, trunk, scar and macrophyllous-leaf evidence into a proposed low-tree reconstruction; it is not a preserved whole specimen. Model selects this hypothesis and retains artistic dimensions, counts, root details and color. Crown/ecobiomorph interpretation remains debated. Copyrighted reconstruction pixels consult-only.

Read track description and anatomy/attribution discussion, especially printed pp282–284. Personally inspected Fig2 actual track map and Fig3 actual field-photo/outline pixels. These support wide gauge, larger pes and strongly asymmetric crescent manus without manual phalanges; no producer genus diagnosis follows. The candidate is a miniature illustrative sequence, not an exact site cast. The file named sauropod-fig2.png is not treated as a figure.

Read diagnosis/description, measurement table and track-A discussion on printed pp423–427. Actual Fig6 photo/map/outline pixels inspected. Strongly asymmetric tridactyl manus has a long posterior digit; selected pes prints are elongate without separated digits or claws. Some prints/sets differ in relative manus/pes placement and preservation; modeled outward/behind manus placement follows illustrative walking-track scope, not the stationary holotype placement or an exact specimen replica.

Read Systematic Ichnology descriptions and discussion of the differing spiral morphologies and inspected actual Fig2 specimens, including O–R, S–U and V–Z. Dense joined masses, spiral sulci and variable tapered/blunter ends support the generic exterior. Three turns, 90mm length, matrix, palette and relief strength are art choices, not copied specimen measurements or a producer/diet diagnosis.

Unavailable full text/source pixels were not treated as inspected by this reviewer and do not support any new detailed assertion. The maker explicitly records an abstract-only Coy1995 route and unavailable2009 full text; accessible original-research2011/2021 substitutions above preserve the broad inventory scope. No denied KU download was retried.

frames.finding: Broad six-paired leaf units are individually recognizable on flattened sprays, with woody taper, visible ascending limbs and a quiet bare lower trunk. The crown is intentionally much airier than the reference painting.
Opposite crown remains spatially open; leafy sprays attach to branch framework rather than floating. Branch/root intersections look like intentional attachment, not exposed coincident faces.
Leaf edges become thin from this direction, but real limbs, woody taper and roots remain clear. This view alone cannot show broad blade shape; top and oblique views do.
Sparse layered branches and edge-on flattened sprays are coherent; no clipped limb or detached blade cluster was seen.
Bare trunk and root spread remain visible. Scaffold angles differ across crown; there is no fern-rosette or floral structure.
Paddle blades and paired arrangement are clear, with real gaps between sprays. Overlapping foliage is normal crown overlap, not a visible coplanar surface defect.
Neutral surface retains blade volume, branches and small scar geometry. No texture or alpha plane is needed to create the identifying structure.
Complete upright tree silhouette with visible flattened spray gaps and root flare; no clipping. It does not independently establish exact leaf dimensions.

frames.finding: One substantial tapered body has broad shallow winding sulci. It is not a loose rope, stack of open rings or shell aperture; the central belly sits into the support.
Blunt circular termination is filled and the opposite winding surface remains connected. The end cap is a stylized flatter end, not an internal cutaway claim.
Continuous body shows broad turns and an extended taper. The central underside touches the matrix while the taper and sulci can clear it naturally.
End-on projection reads as a filled, roughly elliptical section with solid body contact. No through-hole or separate spiral cord is visible.
Reverse profile retains connected relief and visible central contact, with tapered tip raised as part of the same body rather than detached.
Long solid core, three winding divisions and two different end shapes read clearly. Broad relief, not painted bands, supplies the spiral.
Neutral surface still displays the helical sulci, solid core and taper. No coincident-surface flicker or artificial color stripe is needed.
Solid body silhouette joins the matrix at its belly. No full-body hovering gap, disconnected coil or clipping was seen.
